correctness.rationale: Write U for the common product image and P,Q for the separate images of A,B. Since B(P)=U and its kernel on P contains U, dim P>=2r, and symmetrically dim Q>=2r. Square-zero gives the opposite bounds and P=ker A, Q=ker B. Now ker(B|P)=P intersect Q=U, and both products kill P+Q, a 3r-space, so their kernels are exactly that space. Choose W complementary to P+Q. Then A(W),B(W) complement U in P,Q, and AB:W→U is an isomorphism. Transferring a basis of W gives the displayed matrices with H=(AB)^{-1}BA on the quotient; change of basis acts by similarity. Commutation determines the other columns from the W column (R,S,T,P0): they are (P0,0,0,0), (T,P0,0,0) and (HS,0,P0,0). The only constraint is P0H=HP0, and invertibility is exactly that of P0. Summing the orbit counts over invertible similarity classes uses the GL_r class equation. Independently, with A fixed, choose U in P of dimension r, then Q/U complementary to P/U in A^{-1}(U)/U: the respective counts are Gaussian(2r,r) and q^{r²}. Choose the isomorphism V/Q→Q inducing B and sending (P+Q)/Q onto U, giving q^{r²}|GL_r|² choices. The product is q^{r²}|GL_{2r}|, as claimed. These arguments are characteristic-free and give the stated 2520 and 898560. The frozen small-field and centralizer checks were inspected, not run.
